title: Implications of Strong Singapore Dollar on Monetary Authority of Singapore's Losses, Exposure to Investment Risks and Moves to Encourage Higher Level of Savings
what_it_is: Implications of Strong Singapore Dollar on Monetary Authority of Singapore's Losses, Exposure to Investment Risks and Moves to Encourage Higher Level of Savings

sections.label: Questions on MAS losses
sections.summary: Questions asked the Prime Minister about benefits of a strong Singapore dollar policy, MAS's S$30.8 billion losses, their sources, and whether MAS plans higher Treasury Bill and bond yields.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister what were the benefits of a strong Singapore dollar policy that recorded S$30.8 billion in losses last year by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister how much of the reported losses by MAS for FY 2022/2023 are attributable to (i) losses from currency interventions, (ii) changes in valuation, (iii) investment exposures and (iv) other sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister in order to maintain a strong Singapore dollar policy and to curb losses, whether MAS has plans to increase the interest yields and payments of its Treasury Bills and bonds so as to encourage a higher level of savings.

sections.label: Currency translation loss cause
sections.summary: About 70% of the net loss was due to negative currency translation effects of a stronger Singapore dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: About 70% of the net loss was due to the negative currency translation effects of a stronger Singapore dollar.

sections.label: Money market interest expenses
sections.summary: The remaining 30% of the net loss was due to net interest expenses from MAS' money market operations to mop up excess liquidity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The remaining 30% of the net loss was due to net interest expenses from MAS' money market operations to mop up excess liquidity in the banking system.

sections.label: Core inflation fell
sections.summary: On a month-on-month seasonally adjusted annualised basis, MAS' Core Inflation fell from 9.1% in June 2022 to 2.2% in June 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On a month-on-month seasonally adjusted annualised basis, MAS' Core Inflation fell from its peak of 9.1% in June 2022 to 2.2% in June 2023.

sections.label: MAS contribution and budget impact
sections.summary: MAS will contribute S$0.4 billion to the Consolidated Fund this financial year based on past profits, and the smoothening formula mitigated the net loss's budget impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Nonetheless, MAS will still make a contribution of S$0.4 billion to the Government's Consolidated Fund in the current financial year, based on past profits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This smoothening formula has thus helped to mitigate the impact of MAS' net loss on the Government's budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong stated in this House on 1 August 2022, the Government does not expect MAS to deviate from its mandate to maximise its contributions to the Budget.

sections.label: Monetary policy and inflation
sections.summary: Without MAS tightening monetary policy, quarterly core inflation would have peaked at 7.2% year-on-year, 1.9 percentage points higher than the actual 5.4% peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On its impact on price stability and its impact on inflation, I had mentioned that in my Parliamentary Question reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But let me also explain that if MAS had not tightened monetary policy, quarterly core inflation would have reached 7.2% year-on-year at its peak – 1.9 percentage points higher than the actual peak of 5.4% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2023.

sections.label: MAS intervention and Singapore dollar
sections.summary: MAS sold Singapore dollars to moderate the appreciation rate amid high savings rates and capital inflows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Because the Singapore dollar was already on an appreciating trend and in addition to high savings rates as well as large volume of capital inflows, MAS also intervened by selling Singapore dollars and, therefore, moderating the appreciation rate.

sections.label: Import price index fall
sections.summary: Between May 2022 and June 2023, the import price index fell by about 14%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Again, I said that between May 2022 and June 2023, our import price index had fallen by some 14%.

sections.label: MAS investment gains
sections.summary: MAS averaged S$11.7 billion annual investment gain over 15 years and 3.7% over 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Including this latest year, MAS recorded an annual average investment gain of S$11.7 billion in the last 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS seeks to preserve the external purchasing power of the OFR over the long term to support monetary policy implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, over a 20-year period, MAS' average annual investment gain was 3.7%.
